title: Over-Extraction of Trivial or Complexly-Coupled Code Snippets
pattern: Factoring out tiny (1-2 lines) or highly environment-coupled code blocks into a separate helper function, resulting in a method signature with an excessive count of parameters.
why_bad: It increases complexity and cognitive load. The signature of the extracted method is more complex than the original inline duplicate code, forcing future readers to track complex state passing.
detection: An extracted helper method having a high count of arguments (especially mutable references) relative to its total line count.
counterexample: Pure functions that perform mathematically heavy, named formulas with no environmental side-effects.
source: *A Philosophy of Software Design*, Chapter 9.3: "Bring together to eliminate duplication", p. 62, 186.
